items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: I said Dizzy Gillespie and Louis Jordan broke up the big bands. Dizzy Gillespie had a big band and the people couldn't dance to his music.

ctx.x: was playing. But all three of us had teachers. Did you have a band with Clarence Ford?

Oh yeah, yeah. That's when I came out of the service. We had also created by Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker. I called all the old musicians up whom I played with and told them I didn't want to play with them no more. That's because the music you're playing is old, that's out of style. I'm playing bebop now. So Clarence Ford, we graduated from high school together. From Booker T. Washington? Yeah, same class. And Wilbur Hogan too. Did you have him? Yeah. Wilbur Hogan? Yeah. We graduated together. And he, what…
You were talking about Clarence Ford and you know how?

items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1975-05-15
items.q: Dizzy Gillespie got his from Roy Eldridge.

ctx.x: You don't think he was just a clown?

No, indeed not. No, indeed. Often, what would trumpet playing be like today had it not been for Louis Armstrong? Yes. See, because Roy Eldridge got his inspiration from Ray Allen and Louis Armstrong. Which Ray Allen got his inspiration for Louis Armstrong. Dizzy Gillespie got his from Roy Eldridge. Miles Davis got his from...
Dizzy Gillespie. And he went on up to Freddie Hubbard. You know, I think those guys listen to Lester, too. Yeah. Because they get a cool sound like Lester Young.
